chunk_findings.detail: The output file path is deterministic per `(item, gate)` — `.ddflow/local/reviews/<item>.<gate>.jsonl` — and `add` opens it with mode `"w"` on the first chunk of *every* `_ReplyFile` instance (`self._started` is per-instance). So each review run truncates the artifact recorded by the previous run. Concrete sequence: run A reviews all 6 chunks, records gate evidence with `output_file=.ddflow/local/reviews/T1.critic.jsonl` and `output_digest=H1`; the user then runs the advertised re-review `ddflow review T1 --gate critic --chunk 3` (README line ~1113). The new `_ReplyFile`'s first `add` truncates the file and writes only chunk 3's reply, so `H1` no longer matches the file and chunks 1,2,4,5,6 replies referenced by run A's evidence are gone. Worse, if the re-review is refused, the code "is refused WITHOUT recording" (the ERROR/cut-mismatch path), so no new evidence is written while the old file has *already* been truncated before the outcome was known — i.e. a failed re-review silently destroys the prior run's persisted findings, which is exactly the data-loss failure this change exists to prevent. The write should only truncate when there is no previously recorded artifact to preserve (e.g. append/merge keyed by chunk, or write to a fresh run-scoped filename).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py (`_ReplyFile.add` / `_ReplyFile.__init__`)

chunk_findings.detail: The mutual exclusion is a per-instance `threading.Lock`, which gives no protection across processes writing the same deterministic path. The motivating incident is a review that outlives its caller (client aborts at 1800 s, review continues to 2055 s); a natural reaction is to retry the same `ddflow review T1 --gate critic`, producing two concurrent writers to `T1.critic.jsonl`. Because the second process enters with `_started=False`, its first write opens the same file in `"w"` mode and truncates it under the still-running first process, and both then append independently — the recorded `output_digest` will not correspond to any single run's replies. A lock keyed on the path (or an O_EXCL/unique-run filename with the digest taken at close) is needed for the file to be trustworthy evidence under the very interleaving the change targets.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py (`_ReplyFile._lock`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The stated purpose of the progress notification is to reset a client idle timer *during* a review that can run for ~2000 s (B190: 2055 s, client aborted at 1800 s). The test cannot observe when the notifications are emitted relative to the work, because the fake reviewer (`_setup`, `cli.write_text`) returns instantly and completes in a single chunk, and `srv.handle(...)` is synchronous. An implementation that collects notifications and flushes them all in one batch at the end of `handle()` — i.e. exactly the behaviour that leaves the client idle-timing out after 1800 s — still produces `sent = [{"method": "notifications/progress", "params": {"progressToken": "tok", "progress": 1}}]` and passes every assertion (`assert sent`, the `method` check, the `progressToken` check, and the monotonically-increasing `progress` check, which for one chunk is trivially satisfied). So the regression this change exists to prevent (no notification until the review finishes) can silently come back while this test stays green. Demonstrating it requires either a fake reviewer that blocks between chunks (e.g. sleeps/waits on a file, with the test asserting the notification arrives before the reviewer is released) or an assertion on ordering/streaming rather than on the post-hoc notification list.

No other defect I can substantiate from this diff: the digest/body assertions, the relative-path assertion and the no-token case are consistent with the intent, and the shell/TOML setup is well-formed.

chunk_findings.detail: The path is fixed as `<repo>/.ddflow/local/reviews/<item>.<gate>.jsonl` and is opened with mode `"w"` on the first `add` of every `_ReplyFile` instance (`self._started` starts `False`), so any existing content for that item+gate is truncated even when only a subset of chunks is being reviewed. The documented re-review path `ddflow review T1 --gate critic --chunk 2,5` (README) creates a fresh `keep = _ReplyFile(repo, item, gate)` and calls `keep.add` only for chunks 2 and 5; the first call truncates the file that held chunks 1,3,4,6. Two concrete consequences: (1) the gate evidence recorded by the earlier full run stored `output_digest` over the six-chunk file, and after the re-review that digest no longer matches the file it names, so the recorded evidence is not verifiable; (2) `keep.evidence()` is then merged into the *new* gate evidence as `output_file`/`output_digest`, but that file now contains only chunks 2 and 5, so the findings for chunks 1,3,4,6 — the exact bodies this change exists to preserve — are gone from the file the evidence points at. The prior coverage merge (`prior['coverage']`) additionally means the evidence can claim coverage of all chunks while the referenced output file holds only the re-reviewed ones.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_keep` forwards a settled chunk's reply to `on_chunk` only when BOTH `got[0]` is truthy AND `got[1]` is empty (`if on_chunk and got[0] and not got[1]:`). `_race`/`on_settled` hands the callback a `(reply, error)` pair, and the new docstring's stated contract is that `on_chunk(n, reply)` gets "each chunk's whole reply the moment it arrives" so the caller can "keep the finding bodies even if the run is cut short". A chunk that emits findings and then settles with a non-empty second slot (e.g. `("...findings body...", "timeout")` or any degradation/truncation note) is silently dropped: `_keep` returns without ever invoking `on_chunk`, so those bodies never reach the gate evidence/output_file and B190 (evidence holding only finding titles) reproduces for exactly the cut-short chunks this change exists to protect. The guard should only require that a reply is present (e.g. `if on_chunk and got[0]:`); as written it reintroduces the loss for any chunk that carries a reply together with an error annotation.

Note also that the repackaged `on_settled` lambda now returns the tuple `(_keep(...), progress.settled(...))` instead of `progress.settled(...)`'s value, but I could not demonstrate a concrete failure from that without seeing `_race`, so I am not reporting it.

chunk_findings.detail: The test can only ever drive a single review chunk: `_setup` configures one reviewer (`hedge = 1`) and one one-line changed file (`a.py`), so the fake reviewer is invoked once. The only progress assertion is `[f["params"]["progress"] for f in sent] == list(range(1, len(sent) + 1))`, whose right-hand side is computed *from the number of notifications that were actually sent*. It is therefore satisfied by any implementation that emits a single notification, or that queues every progress frame and flushes them only after `srv.handle` returns. The failure mode this change exists to fix (B190: 2055 s / 6 chunks, client aborted at 1800 s because no *intermediate* progress notification reset the idle timer) requires ≥2 chunks with the notification arriving between chunks; with one chunk the test passes even if no progress is emitted until the whole review is over, so the regression can silently recur. A reviewer that returns two findings across two changed files (or a forced multi-chunk review) plus an assertion that a progress frame is observed while the review is still in flight would actually pin the behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The new "run" discriminator is `time.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')` (1-second resolution) plus `os.getpid()`, so it is not unique within a process. Two `ReviewRecorder`s constructed for the same `item`+`gate` in the same second get the identical `self.path`. The docstring explicitly claims this prevents "a retry of an aborted call running at the same time" from truncating the earlier record's file, but a retry handled by the same (threaded) MCP server process in the same wall-clock second produces the same path; each recorder has its own `threading.Lock`, so the two writers either truncate/overwrite or interleave partial JSONL lines, and the `output_digest` saved in the first record no longer matches `path.read_bytes()`. The regression test added in this same diff demonstrates the collision directly: it calls `api.review(repo, gate="critic", item="T1")` twice in a row in one process and then asserts `Path(_gate(repo).evidence["output_file"]) != path`; with a fast in-process fake reviewer both `__init__`s fall in the same second and `getpid()` is equal, so the paths are identical and both that assertion and the digest assertion fail. A counter (or uuid, or same-second disambiguation) is needed for the guarantee the comment states to actually hold.
